subject.title: fix: stabilize OpenClaw beta setup and PT-PT formatting

question: Should the Windows Companion default to `2026.7.2-beta.2` even though the exact published artifact is documented here as failing the native-wizard path until an open upstream fix ships?
rationale: The patch can be mechanically revised, but choosing a prerelease as the supported default despite a known upstream runtime dependency is a release-policy choice rather than an implementation detail.

options.title: Wait for a published, proven artifact
options.body: Keep the default on the existing supported target until the upstream wizard fix is published and exact-artifact setup proof succeeds.

options.title: Accept the beta default deliberately
options.body: Approve the prerelease default with the documented first-run Gateway-loss risk and an explicit support/recovery plan.

options.title: Split the independent fixes
options.body: Move the locale and Companion lifecycle work forward separately while deferring the version-default decision.

recommendation.title: Wait for a published, proven artifact
recommendation.body: Keep the default on the existing supported target until the upstream wizard fix is published and exact-artifact setup proof succeeds.
